crash_dump_00000006.dmp -- C3D_BindProgram dereferencing the shader program the
menu had just freed.

Resolved against 3DAlpha-a1.1.2.elf in this directory, which is the binary that
ran (archived before the fix was built).

ARM11 core 0, data abort
  pc   = 0x0013DC9C   C3D_BindProgram, citro3d 1.7.1 base.c:369
  far  = 0x00001008
  dfsr = 0x00000005   translation fault (section), on READ
  sp   = 0x08007588   2,696 bytes into a 32 KB stack -- not an overflow

The three instructions before pc, out of the dump's own code window:

  0x0013DC8C  E59CE000  ldr lr,  [r12]      @ oldProg->vertexShader  = 0x08010AA0
  0x0013DC94  E59EC000  ldr r12, [lr]       @ ...->dvle              = 0x00001000
  0x0013DC9C  E59CC008  ldr r12, [r12, #8]  @ <-- fault, reads 0x1008

r12 came from `ldr r12, [r1, #0x24]` at 0x0013DC50, which is `C3D_Context::program`
-- the **previously** bound program, not the one being bound. citro3d reads it on
every bind to decide whether the geometry-shader mode has to change, and it does
so before it touches the new program at all.

The previously bound program was citro2d's. `Menu::shutdown` called `C2D_Fini`,
whose disassembly is `C3D_FrameEndHook(0,0)`, `shaderProgramFree`, `DVLB_Free`,
two `linearFree`s -- so citro2d's `shaderInstance_s` at 0x08010AA0 was returned to
the newlib heap and its `dvle` field is now allocator metadata (0x00001000).
citro3d was never told, and kept the pointer.

Call chain, from the return addresses in the 2,680-byte stack dump:

  sp+0x02E0  0x0010385C  main                      main.cpp:552   (runShell inlined)
  sp+0x02E4  0x001028EC  runGame                   main.cpp:510   renderer.drawFrame
             0x001096B8  Renderer::drawEye         renderer.cpp:667
             0x001090C8  Renderer::drawPass        renderer.cpp:602
  sp+0x0004  0x001085E4  Renderer::bindPipeline    renderer.cpp:212
             0x0013DC9C  C3D_BindProgram           <-- fault

So the world had opened -- "World2" is still in main's frame at 0x08007FB0 as an
SSO std::string -- the renderer had initialised, and the crash is the first draw
call of the first frame. `renderer.init()` does not bind anything; `buildPipeline`
only parses and inits. The first bind in the process after the menu tore citro2d
down is this one.

**The rule this was missing, and it is symmetric.** Freeing a shader program
leaves citro3d holding a corpse, and the fault lands on whoever binds next rather
than on the code that did the freeing. The menu freeing citro2d's program takes
down the game's first frame; `Renderer::shutdown` freeing its three pipelines
would have taken down the menu on the way back, one lap later. Nothing warns
about either.

Fixed by `ctr::parkShaderProgram()` (renderer.hpp): a program built once from the
world shader and never freed, bound immediately before either side frees
anything, so the next bind always dereferences something alive. Called from
`Renderer::shutdown` and `Menu::shutdown`. The one place that legitimately does
not need it is a free immediately followed by `C3D_Fini`, which throws the
context and its pointer away together -- the M0 probe's teardown.
